title.narrative: Life-saving Agriculture and Nutrition-sensitive Assistance to Crisis affected populations in Local Government Areas in BAY states

description.narrative: The project focuses on Life-saving Agriculture and Nutrition-sensitive Assistance to Crisis affected populations in Local Government Areas in BAY states. The project will provide emergency agriculture assistance including agricultural inputs and micro-gardening kits to 4,000 most-vulnerable households and dry Season food production to 9000 households. This will be complemented by establishing and manage 10 Farmer Field Schools (FFS), to build capacities of approximately 300 farmers and disseminate knowledge and best practices in areas such as climate smart agricultures. FAO will use a Twin Track approach with WFP to reach the same households benefitting from food assistance and protect the productive agriculture assets provided. In addition, in partnership with UNICEF, and through this project FAO will support efforts to prevent relapse of acute malnutrition by providing “Tom Brown”, a locally produced supplementary food (LPSF), to 2100 children under-5 that have recovered from Severe Acute Malnutrition.. To increase local availability of Tom Brown, the project will support four existing Tom Brown production centres to scale up production. Moreover, the project will train four women’s cooperative groups in the recipe and formulation of Tom Brown using locally-available cereals and pulses, further increasing its availability. Overall, the project will directly reach 65100 people.
